issues: McNemar test is uninformative (b=c=0, p=1.0) due to threshold degeneracy (threshold=1.000001) for both B02 and B08, preventing statistical differentiation of F1-scores.
The sample size of N=744 test pairs is slightly underpowered compared to the Phase 1 target of N=800 pairs required for 80% power at d=0.3 at the Bonferroni-corrected alpha level of 0.0017.
Bootstrap confidence intervals are wide relative to effect sizes (e.g., SBG AUROC CI spans 0.097, Best baseline CI spans 0.085), indicating borderline medium effect (Cohen's d ≈ 0.45).

E3 permutation test for variance difference yields p=1.0 because the observed variance difference is in the opposite direction of the H3 claim (SP_std > SC_std), showing that refactoring transforms are actually more variable than mutations.

primary_metrics: AUROC (primary, threshold-independent due to degeneracy risks)
F1-score (evaluated using thresholds optimized on DEV split only)
Cohen's d / Glass's delta (for continuous comparisons and variance stability)
Cohen's h (for difference in proportions / F1-score comparisons)

H7.description: Dynamic behavioral genomes achieve higher discrimination (AUROC) than static genomes on test set.
H7.statistical_test: Paired McNemar test on predictions (using thresholds set on DEV split) and bootstrap AUROC comparison.

H8.description: Hybrid representations (static + dynamic) achieve higher discrimination (AUROC) than pure dynamic representations on test set.
H8.statistical_test: Paired McNemar test on predictions (using thresholds set on DEV split) and bootstrap AUROC comparison.

H9.description: Dynamic behavioral representations reduce structural-semantic inversion by showing significantly higher delta(EQUIV_mean - CHANGED_mean) compared to static behavioral representations.
H9.statistical_test: Paired permutation test on the difference of deltas between dynamic and static representation pairs.

H10.description: Dynamic and hybrid representations exhibit robustness (retaining discrimination power) across code noise levels.
H10.statistical_test: Friedman-like permutation analog test across noise levels to evaluate robustness.

H11.description: Behavioral genomes achieve high matching accuracy on cross-language equivalents (Python vs Java).
H11.statistical_test: Paired McNemar test on cross-language pairs, explicitly acknowledging small n (n=15) and reporting low statistical power.

H12.description: The SBG v2 system detects regression behavior with AUROC significantly exceeding the best structural baseline.
H12.statistical_test: AUROC comparison with 1000-resample bootstrap confidence intervals.

sample_size_assessment.recommendation_v2: To maintain 80% power under the stricter Holm-Bonferroni correction at alpha=0.000833, expand the test split to at least 1000 pairs (or at least 1280 pairs to provide a conservative margin).
